name: Hermann Ludwig Ferdinand von Helmholtz
summary: German physicist and physiologist known for contributions to physiological optics, color vision, and invention of the ophthalmoscope.

name: Nicholas J. Wade
summary: Author of the source document, affiliated with the Department of Psychology, University of Dundee.

name: University of Dundee
summary: University in Scotland, UK, where the author Nicholas J. Wade is affiliated.

name: Journal of the History of the Neurosciences
aliases: JOURNAL OF THE HISTORY OF THE NEUROSCIENCES
summary: Academic journal publishing the source document.

name: University of Königsberg
summary: University where Helmholtz delivered his inaugural lecture in 1852.

name: University of Bonn
summary: University where Helmholtz worked during his academic progression.

name: University of Heidelberg
summary: University where Helmholtz worked and conducted experiments on binocular vision in the early 1860s.

name: University of Berlin
summary: University where Helmholtz progressed to later in his career.

name: Optical Society of America
summary: Organization that commissioned the English translation of Helmholtz's Handbuch in 1921.

name: Handbuch der physiologischen Optik
summary: Helmholtz's major work on physiological optics, published in parts and later as a single volume.

name: Treatise on Physiological Optics
summary: English translation of Helmholtz's Handbuch, translated by James Powell Cocke Southall.

name: Ophthalmoscope
summary: Instrument invented by Helmholtz for examining the retina in the living eye.

name: Ophthalmometer
summary: Instrument invented by Helmholtz for measuring changes in lens curvature.

name: Telestereoscope
summary: Reflecting stereoscope invented by Helmholtz to enhance disparities.

name: Johannes Müller
summary: Helmholtz's mentor, proposed theory of specific nerve energies.

name: Ewald Hering
summary: Physiologist who had conflicts with Helmholtz over theories of vision.

name: Charles Wheatstone
summary: Inventor of the stereoscope, whose work Helmholtz acknowledged.

name: James Powell Cocke Southall
summary: Translator of Helmholtz's Treatise on Physiological Optics into English.

name: Arthur König
summary: Editor of the final part of the second edition of Helmholtz's Handbuch.

name: Willibald Nagel
summary: Editor of the third edition of Helmholtz's Handbuch.

name: Allvar Gullstrand
summary: Editor of the third edition of Helmholtz's Handbuch.

name: Johannes von Kries
summary: Editor of the third edition of Helmholtz's Handbuch.

name: Max Planck
summary: Student of Helmholtz who laid foundations for quantum theory.

name: Thomas Young
summary: Physician and physicist whose trichromatic theory Helmholtz supported.

name: James Clerk Maxwell
summary: Physicist whose color disc experiments supported Helmholtz's color theory.

name: Archiv für Ophthalmologie
summary: Journal created essentially by the invention of the ophthalmoscope.
